title: Quadratic gate constraints become a cubic-Hamiltonian symplectic fixed-locus retract

statement.quantifiers: Every affine scheme X of finite presentation over Z; choose its finite arithmetic circuit, introduce uniquely evaluated gate variables and quadratic defining constraints Q_i(z).
statement.assertion: For H=sum_i lambda_i Q_i and F(q,p)=(q,p-grad H(q)), F is an integer quadratic polynomial symplectic automorphism and X is a scheme-theoretic retract of Fix(F) over every commutative ring.
assumptions: All gate equations plus original output constraints included; integer coefficient arithmetic circuit exact.
q=(z,lambda); section sets lambda=p=0, projection returns z satisfying Q_i=0.
Fixed dimension for one universal Diophantine circuit only; arbitrary X has variable circuit dimension.

inputs: Finite integral polynomial presentation and arithmetic circuit.
outputs: Quadratic map/inverse, cubic autonomous Hamiltonian, complete affine-in-time flow and exact all-ring retraction.
interface.precision: Exact algebraic identities, no numerical flow or finite-precision undecidability claim.
costs: Gate count, coefficient lengths and dense polynomial output charged; no witness finder.
The specified universal integer-hard family supplies a rational fixed point on every input via s=1/2; the universal polynomial/circuit is not instantiated in the packet.

proof_mechanism: Normalize polynomial equations to unique quadratic addition/multiplication gate constraints.
Multiplier derivatives of H are Q_i; the z derivatives are sum lambda_i partial_z Q_i.
A gradient momentum shear preserves the canonical symplectic form by Hessian symmetry; inverse negates the momentum increment.
Fix(F) has ideal(Q_i,sum lambda_i partial_z Q_i); projection and zero-multiplier section compose to identity.
Choosing one universal U(t,x) and W=U(t,x)(2s-1), with Q0=t-n, yields F_n=F0+n e in one fixed dimension, integer fixed points iff n belongs to the universal c.e. set, rational section always exists.
obstructions: The entire fixed locus need not be isomorphic to X or a product; only the retract is proved.
Integer undecidability uses classical DPRM/Jones and is unconditional; rational undecidability needs a separate unverified H10(Q) theorem.
No chaos, trajectory-computation hardness, compact/Floer construction or physical energy bound follows.

potential_uses.target: Exact arithmetic constraints inside geometric maps
potential_uses.transfer_gate: Separate algebraic representation from dynamical hardness, fixed from variable dimension, and integer from rational solvability.

review.source_reported: Source-scoped analytic derivations, independent reconstruction for counting/logarithm, and finite checks reported; Hamiltonian proof has source-reported review only; no independent ingestion proof reconstruction, scientific replay, external correctness or priority clearance.
